Rashi on Zevachim 8b:3:1.hebrew: שלא לשמו פסול - כדאמרינן (לעיל זבחים דף ז:):
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:3:1.english: **Not for its sake, it is unfit:** As we say (above, Zevachim 7b).

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:3:2.hebrew: בשאר ימות השנה לשמו פסול - כדאמרינן במסכת פסחים (דף סא.) שחטו קודם חצות פסול דכתיב "בין הערבים", וכמה פעמים שנה הכתוב בקביעות זמנו בי"ד "בין הערבים":
Rashi on Zevachim 8b:3:2.english: **During the rest of the days of the year, for its sake, it is unfit:** As we say in Tractate Pesachim (61a): If one slaughtered it before midday, it is unfit, as it is written "between the evenings." And the verse repeated several times the fixed time of its sacrifice on the fourteenth "between the evenings."

Rashi on Zevachim 8b:3:3.english: **Not for its sake, it is fit:** As it explains further on.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:11:1.hebrew: הא חי - אם שחטה בשינוי בעלים לשם אדם חי:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:11:1.english: But a living [person] - If one slaughtered it with a change of owner, for the sake of a living person:

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:11:2.hebrew: דומיא דנחשון - שמחוייב חטאת שאינה על חטא, הדומה לשעיר נחשון, כגון חטאת נזיר ומצורע הבאות להכשיר — פסולה:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:11:2.english: Similar to Nahshon - [If it was slaughtered for] one who is obligated to bring a sin offering that is not for a sin, similar to the he-goat of Nahshon, such as the sin offering of a nazirite or a leper, which are brought to render [them] fit — it is unfit.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:12:1.hebrew: ופרכינן הני עולות נינהו - ואנן קים לן לעיל (זבחים דף ז.), חטאת ששחטה על מי שמחוייב עולה כשירה, והני כעולה דמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:12:1.english: And we ask: These are burnt offerings - But we have established earlier (Zevachim 7a) that a sin offering slaughtered for the sake of one who is obligated to bring a burnt offering is valid, and these [sin offerings of the nazirite and the leper] are considered like a burnt offering:

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:12:2.english: Pashita ("It is obvious") - We do not have this in the text.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:15:1.hebrew: עיקר חטאת נקט - שורש החטאת, שהיא היתה חטאת יחיד ראשונה:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:15:1.english: He cited the primary sin offering - The root of the sin offering, as it was the first individual sin offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:16:1.hebrew: לשם חטאת עבודת כוכבים - רבותא נקט, אע"ג דלא דמיא לשאר חטאות, שהן בכבשה או שעירה, והיא אינה כשירה בכבשה אלא בשעירה:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:16:1.english: For the sake of a sin offering of idol worship - He stated a novelty, even though it is not similar to the other sin offerings, which may be [brought] from a ewe-lamb or a she-goat, whereas this one is not valid from a ewe-lamb but only from a she-goat.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:18:1.hebrew: מי אמרינן כרת כמותה - והוה ליה מחוייב כפרה כמותו, וקרינן ביה "עליו" ולא על חבירו, וחבירו דומיא דידיה? או דילמא כו', דאין קבוע כמותו שבא בעולה ויורד:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:18:1.english: Do we say [that] karet is like it? - Is he then one obligated to bring atonement like it (the chatat of chelev), and do we read in it "for him" (alav), and not for his fellow, [meaning that] his fellow is similar to him? Or perhaps etc., since a fixed [offering] is not like it, [being an offering] that comes as an olah v'yored (a sliding-scale offering):

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:1:1.english: Its time has passed - The time of the slaughter of the Paschal offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:21:1.hebrew: בעיא דרבא היכי מתניתו לה - וכיון דאמרת דרבא בכולהו פסיל, ואפילו חטאת חלב לשם חטאת דם, כ"ש לשם חטאת דטומאת מקדש וקדשיו:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:21:1.english: Rava’s dilemma — how do you teach it? - Since you say [according to] Rava that [slaughter for the sake of another sin offering] disqualifies in all of them, and even a fat-sin-offering [slaughtered] for the sake of a blood-sin-offering, all the more so [if slaughtered] for the sake of the sin offering for defilement of the Temple and its sacred things:

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:22:1.hebrew: לשם חטאת עבודת כוכבים - רבותא נקט, אע"ג דלא דמיא לשאר חטאות, שהן בכבשה או שעירה, והיא חטאת עבודת כוכבים אינה כשירה בכבשה אלא בשעירה:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:22:1.english: For the sake of an idol-worship sin offering - He stated a novelty, even though it is not similar to the other sin offerings, which may be brought from a ewe-lamb or a female goat, whereas it [the idol-worship sin offering] is not valid from a ewe-lamb but only from a female goat:

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:25:1.hebrew: שחטה לשמה - שלא חישב על השחיטה, אלא על הזריקה חישב בשעת שחיטה, דהיינו מעבודה לעבודה:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:25:1.english: He slaughtered it for its sake - That is, he did not have the improper intent during the slaughter itself; rather, he had the intent concerning the sprinkling at the time of the slaughter, which is [an intent] from one service to another service.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:26:1.hebrew: מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה - כלומר, מחשבה מועלת מעבודה לעבודה, במחשבת שלא לשמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:26:1.english: One can have intention from rite to rite - That is, intention is effective from one rite to another, with intention of [offering it] not for its own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:26:2.hebrew: דילפינן ממחשבת פיגול - דמהניא ביה הכי, דתנן בפרק שני (לקמן זבחים דף כז:): השוחט את הזבח על מנת לזרוק דמו למחר — פיגול:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:26:2.english: We derive from intent of piggul - For [such intent] is effective in it in this way, as we learned in the second chapter (below, Zevachim 27b): One who slaughters the sacrifice with the intent to throw its blood tomorrow — [it is] piggul.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:27:1.hebrew: אין מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה - בשלא לשמו, דלא ילפינן לה מפיגול. דהתם עיקר מחשבתו המביאה לידי פיגול זו היא, שיחשוב בעבודה זו לעשות עבודה אחרת מן אחת העבודות, להאכיל לאדם או למזבח חוץ לזמנו — וזריקה אכילת מזבח היא. והוא הדין אם חישב על הקטרת החלב, שאינה מן עבודות. הילכך לא דמיא לשלא לשמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:27:1.english: One cannot have intention from one rite to another rite - Regarding [an offering slaughtered] not for its own sake, [Reish Lakish holds] that we do not derive it from piggul. For there, the essential thought that brings about piggul is this: that during this rite he thinks to perform another rite, from among the rites, in order to feed a person or the altar [the offering] outside its proper time — and sprinkling is the altar's eating. And the same law applies if he had intent regarding the burning of the fats, which is not one of the rites. Therefore, it is not comparable to [an offering brought] not for its own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:3:1.hebrew: לא זמנו ולא שנתו - ואם שחטו קודם הפסח לשם שלמים, כשר, ואע"ג דחזי לפסח ראשון:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:3:1.english: Neither its time nor its year - And if one slaughtered it before Passover for the sake of peace offerings, it is valid, even though it is fit for the first Passover.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:3:2.english: From their status - From the first Paschal offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:4:1.english: In the name of Mavog - Mavog is the name of a Sage.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:4:2.english: A sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering of Nahshon - [This refers to] the goat sin offering of the dedication of the princes:

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:4:3.hebrew: כשרה - ולא הויא שינוי קדש, דלא אמרי' חטאת נחשון, כיון דלדורון אתי ולא לכפרה על חטא, הרי היא כשחיטה לשם עולה. וכ"ש דשינוי בעלים לא הוי, דלא שחטה להתכפר בה נחשון:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:4:3.english: Fit - And it is not a change of sanctity, for we do not say "a sin offering of Nahshon," since it comes as a gift and not as atonement for a sin; it is therefore like slaughtering it for the sake of a burnt offering. And all the more so, it is not a change of owner, for he did not slaughter it so that Nahshon would be atoned through it.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:5:1.hebrew: ועלו לבעלים - ר"ש פליג אמנחות, ומודה בזבחים:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:5:1.english: And they satisfied the obligation of the owners - Rabbi Shimon disagrees with regard to meal offerings, and concedes with regard to animal offerings.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:6:1.hebrew: מחבת ומרחשת - שני כלים שבהם מטגנים את המנחות. שכל המנחות היו נעשות עשר עשר חלות. מחבת — צפה, ומעשיה קשים: מתוך שהכלי צף, מעשיה מתפשטין, והאור שורף את השמן. מרחשת — עמוקה, ומעשיה רוחשין ורכין, שאין האור שורף את השמן, וכשמניח אדם אצבעו עליה נראה כמו רוחשת:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:6:1.english: Machavat and marcheshet - These are two vessels in which meal offerings are fried. For all the meal offerings were made ten loaves each. The machavat is shallow, and its contents are hard: since the vessel is shallow, its contents spread out, and the fire burns the oil. The marcheshet is deep, and its contents are seething and soft, since the fire does not burn the oil; and when a person places his finger on it, it appears to be seething.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:6:2.hebrew: חריבה - מנחת חוטא, שאין בה שמן, דכתיב (ויקרא ה) לא ישים עליה שמן:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:6:2.english: Dry - This is the meal offering of a sinner, which has no oil in it, as it is written (Leviticus 5:11): "He shall not put oil upon it."

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:6:3.hebrew: מעשיה מוכיחין - דמחשבה הניכרת שהיא שקר, סבר ר"ש דלא מהניא:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:6:3.english: Its actions prove - For a thought that is evidently false, Rabbi Shimon holds that it is not effective.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:7:1.hebrew: שחיטה אחת לכולן - וכי שחיט עולה לשם חטאת, ליכא הכירא דמשקר. הילכך מהניא מחשבה. כ"ך שמעת"י במנחו"ת:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:7:1.english: One slaughter for all of them - For when one slaughters an burnt offering for the sake of a sin offering, there is no discernible sign that he is lying. Therefore, intention is effective. Thus I heard in Menachot.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:8:1.hebrew: טעמא כו' - אלמא, אפי' לרבי שמעון דמהדר להיכשירא, לא יליף מזאת תורה, וכ"ש דמדרבנן. קשיא לך דאמרי אף במנחות לא עלו? אלמא לא דרשי תורה להכי. ולרבא דאמר לעיל (זבחים דף ז.) חטאת חלב ששחטה לשם חטאת דם כשירה, ליכא למיפרך מינה, דהתם כיון דכי הדדי נינהו, דתרוייהו חטאת סתמא שמייהו, וכפרת שתיהן שוה על הכרת, אין שם שינוי קודש, והרי חטאת לשם חטאת נשחטה. ואילו מנחת מחבת ומנחת מרחשת אין שמותיהן שוין: זו שמה לבדה וזו שמה לבדה. אלא לרב קשיא, דהא לשם חטאת נחשון שינוי גמור הוא, שהרי היא כעולה, וקאמר כשרה משום תורת חטאת:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:8:1.english: The reason, etc. - Evidently, even according to Rabbi Shimon, who seeks to validate [the offering], [the Gemara] does not derive [validity] from "this is the law," and certainly [not according to the Rabbis], who rule only on the basis of rabbinic reasoning. Does it trouble you that they say that even among meal offerings [the offering] did not satisfy the obligation? Evidently, they do not expound "law" for this purpose. And according to Rava, who said earlier (Zevachim 7a) that a fat-bearing sin offering slaughtered for the sake of a blood-bearing sin offering is valid, one cannot refute [his view] from this [case]. For there, since they are the same as one another — both are, by their names, simply "sin offering," and the atonement of both is equal with respect to karet — there is no change of sanctity [designation], and behold, a sin offering was slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering. Whereas the names of a pan-baked meal offering and a deep-pan meal offering are not the same: this one has its own name alone, and that one has its own name alone. But according to Rav it is difficult, for [an offering slaughtered] for the sake of the sin offering of Nachshon is a complete change, since it is like a burnt offering, and yet he says it is valid because of the "law of the sin offering."

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:9:1.hebrew: אלא אי איתמר - מימרא דרב, הכי איתמר, ובשינוי בעלים איתמר:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:9:1.english: Rather, if it was stated - The statement of Rav was stated like this, and it was stated with regard to a change of owner.

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:9:2.english: That he be atoned for by it - This is [considered] a change of owner:

Rashi on Zevachim 9b:9:3.hebrew: שאין כפרה למתים - הילכך לא קרינא ביה ״ובמחוייב כפרה כמותו:
Rashi on Zevachim 9b:9:3.english: For there is no atonement for the dead - Therefore, we do not apply to it [the expression] “one who is obligated in atonement like him”:

Steinsaltz comment #1 on Zevachim 9b:16.english: Rav also mentions this sin offering because there is a certain novelty in it, as an idol worship sin offering differs from other sin offerings in that only a she-goat is sacrificed, and not a ewe-lamb or a ewe-goat as with other sin offerings.

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 9b:16.english: ב Rav says: A sin offering that one designated to atone for consuming chelev, that one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering brought for consuming blood, or for the sake of a sin offering brought for engaging in idol worship — is fit, as this is not a deviation from its original name.

Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:3:1.hebrew: הגה"ה בשאר ימות השנה לשמו פסול - היינו קודם הפסח, דבעי עקירה, או כגון דנדחו בעלים לפסח שני. אבל אחר כך לא, דפסח בשאר ימות השנה שלמים, ושלמים לשם פסח קא שחיט כדאמר בפרק תמיד נשחט (פסחים דף סד.) ובפרק שני דחולין (דף ל.). ומיהו איכא למאן דאמר בסוף אלו דברים (פסחים דף עג:) דבעי עקירה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:3:1.english: **Glosses: During the rest of the days of the year, for its sake, it is unfit:** This refers to before Passover, where it requires uprooting (the original designation), or for example, if the owners were deferred to a second Passover. But afterwards, no, because a Paschal offering during the rest of the year is a peace offering, and one who slaughters a peace offering for the sake of a Paschal offering is fit, as it says in פרק תמיד נשחט (Pesachim 64b) and in פרק שני דחולין (30a). Nevertheless, there is an opinion (at the end of אלו דברים (Pesachim 73b)) that it requires uprooting.

Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:3:2.hebrew: לשמו פסול - (כתוב) בקונטרס דלא חזו למילתייהו. ורבינו שמשון הגיה כדאמר בפסחים (דף סא.) שחטו קודם חצות פסול שנאמר "בין הערבים", וכמה פעמים שנה הכתוב בקביעות זמנו בארבעה עשר "בין הערבים". וסוגיא דהש"ס נמי משמע לקמן בגמרא הפסח ששחטו שחרית דמבין הערבים נפיק. ואין לומר דנפיק מדדרשינן הכא לזבח שלמים שצריך שיעקרנו לזבח שלמים, דדילמא הני מילי למצוה אבל לעכב לא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 8b:3:2.english: **For its sake, it is unfit:** Rashi explains that they are not suitable for their purpose. And Rabbeinu Shimshon annotated that it says in Pesachim (61a) that if one slaughtered it before midday it is unfit, as it is stated "between the evenings," and the verse repeated several times the fixed time of its sacrifice on the fourteenth "between the evenings." And the Gemara's discussion also implies further on in the Gemara, regarding a Paschal offering that was slaughtered in the morning, that it is derived from "between the evenings." And one cannot say that it is derived from what we expounded here, "for a sacrifice of peace offerings," that it must uproot it for a sacrifice of peace offerings, because perhaps these words are for the mitzvah (initially), but not to invalidate.

Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:16:1.english: Rav says: A chelev sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering is fit - Rabbeinu Tam explains that Rabba holds like Rav Ḥisda, for Rabba's [opinion] was refuted. And the reason for a thanks offering for the sake of a peace offering implies that Reish Lakish deals with a case where one slaughtered it for the sake of his friend's sin offering. But it seems that it does not deal with this, since it does not explicitly say "his friend," rather it deals with a chelev sin offering for the sake of a blood sin offering, as Rava says further in this chapter (Zevachim 9b:): a chelev sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a blood sin offering, for the sake of an idol worship sin offering, is fit; for the sake of a nazirite's sin offering, for the sake of a leper's sin offering is unfit, these are burnt offerings. And if you say: why do I need Rabba's two [statements]? It can be said that this one here is stated to teach us that a change of offering is the opposite of a change of owner, even though Rava did not explain the verses according to his words, as he said at the beginning of the chapter (Zevachim 3b) that Rav Yosef bar Ami raises a contradiction about change of offering and resolves it. And the one below states to differentiate between sin offerings, and also because of the subsequent dilemma which Rava asks: a chelev sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a Temple and its holy items defilement sin offering, what is its ruling?

Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:17:1.hebrew: לשם חטאת נזיר לשם חטאת מצורע - לעיל (זבחים דף ז.) איכא שמעתא אחריתי דרב, דמחלק בין שוחט זבח [לשם חטאת] לשוחט לשם עולה. ושם פירשתי תרתי דרבא מה שאמר למה לי:
Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:17:1.english: "For the sake of a nazirite's sin offering, or for the sake of a leper's sin offering" - Above (Zevachim 7a) there is another teaching of Rav, who distinguishes between one who slaughters an offering for the sake of a sin offering and one who slaughters for the sake of a burnt offering. And there I explained [the question of] why I need Rava's two [statements].

Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:20:1.hebrew: ושחט אותה לחטאת - לעיל בפירקין דרשינן ליה למילתא אחריתי. ושמא הכא דריש מדלא כתיב "ושחט לחטאת אותה":
Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:20:1.english: "And slaughter it for a sin offering" - Earlier in this chapter we expounded it for a different matter. And perhaps here [Rav Aḥa son of Rava] expounds it from the fact that it is not written, "And slaughter for a sin offering it [otah]."

Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:20:2.english: Concerning one who is obligated to bring a sin offering for impurity of the Temple and its sacred things, what is the law? - But how is he worse than one who is not obligated to bring anything at all?

Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:26:1.hebrew: מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה - כדאמר, כגון משחיטה לזריקה (כמו שינוי בעלים); אבל משחיטה לקבלה לא, דהא מפיגול יליף לה. וק"ו דרב אשי דיליף משינוי בעלים לא הוי אלא משחיטה לזריקה, כמו שינוי בעלי'. ותימה, דלקמן (זבחים דף יג.) דפריך "וקבלה מי פסלה כו'", ומשני "כאן במחשבת שלא לשמן, כאן במחשבת פיגול", אמאי לא משני אידי ואידי במחשבת שלא לשמן, וקבלה לא עשה בה מחשבה כמעשה, כגון בשוחט על מנת לקבל שלא לשמן, ובזריקה (לא) עשה בה מחשבה כמעשה? ונראה לי דלקמן מיירי שחישב בעבודה עצמה: אם קבל [לגמור הקבלה] שלא לשמן — פסול, ואם קבל [לגמור] חוץ לזמנו — כשר, ואם זרק לגמור הזריקה חוץ לזמנו — פסול. וכן מקטיר לגמור ההקטרה למחר, דהוה פסול אי לאו דמעטיה קרא לקמן משום דאין מעכבת כפרה. אבל ליכא לפרושי לקמן מחשבת פיגול דלא פסלה בקבלה, כגון שוחט על מנת לקבל דמן חוץ לזמנו, דבשלא לשמן נמי לא פסלה, דמעבודה לעבודה ילפינן מפיגול (ואי) במקבל על מנת לזרוק חוץ לזמנו הוה פיגול; אלא כדפרשינן בחישב בעבודה עצמה. ברו"ך. ובלאו הכי תימה, דהוי מצי למימר קבלה לא עשה בה מחשבה כמעשה לענין שינוי בעלים:
Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:26:1.english: One may have intention from one rite to another rite - As [the Gemara] said: for example, from the slaughter to the sprinkling (like a change of owner). But from the slaughter to the receiving, no, since he derives it from piggul. And the kal vaḥomer of Rav Ashi, who derives it from a change of owner, applies only from slaughter to sprinkling, like a change of owner. And it is puzzling: below (Zevachim 13a), where [the Gemara] asks, "And did receiving disqualify?...", and answers, "Here it is with intention of a different designation, there it is with intention of piggul" — why does it not answer that both cases involve intention of a different designation, and with receiving, one did not treat intention as equal to action, for example when one slaughters with the intention to receive for a different designation, whereas with sprinkling one (does not) treat intention as equal to action? And it seems to me that below [the Gemara] speaks of one who had the intention during the rite itself: if he received with intention to complete the receiving for a different designation, it is unfit; if he received with intention to complete [it] outside its time, it is valid; and if he sprinkled with intention to complete the sprinkling outside its time, it is unfit. And similarly one who burns the offering with intention to complete the burning on the next day — it would be unfit were it not that Scripture excluded it below, because it is not indispensable for atonement. But it is impossible to explain the Gemara below as referring to intention of piggul that does not disqualify in the receiving, such as one who slaughters with the intention to receive outside its time, for with a different designation too it does not disqualify, since we derive [intention] from one rite to another from piggul (and if) one who receives with intention to sprinkle outside its time, it would be piggul; rather, it is as we explained, [that he] had the intention during the rite itself. Barukh. And even without this it is puzzling, for it could have said that with receiving, one did not treat intention as equal to action with regard to a change of owner:

Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:2:1.hebrew: חד לעיברה שנתו וזמנו - ה"ה לעיברה שנתו בלא זמנו. ואע"פ שבשעה שהקדישו לא היה ראוי לפסח, דכשיגיע זמנו תעבור שנתו — דאפי' מפריש נקיבה לפסחו או זכר בן שתי שנים, תורת שלמים עליו, כדתנן במי שהיה טמא (פסחים דף צז:): ירעה עד שיסתאב, וימכר ויביא בדמיו שלמים:
Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:2:1.english: One [verse] for a case where its year and its time have passed - The same law applies [to a case where] its year [has passed] without its time. And even though at the time he consecrated it, it was not fit for a Paschal offering, [since] when its time arrives its year will have passed — for even if one designates a female for his Paschal offering, or a male two years old, it has the status of a peace offering, as we learned in the Mishnah regarding one who was impure (Pesachim 97b): It shall graze until it becomes blemished, and it is sold, and he brings peace offerings with the proceeds:

Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:5:1.hebrew: איתיביה רב משרשיא לרבא כו' - תימה: מאי קושיא? הא רבא הוא דמפרש טעמא דר"ש בריש מנחות (דף ג:): "מזאת תורת". ואומר ר"ת דהכא גרסי' "רבה", ורבה לטעמיה, דמשני התם: כאן בשינוי קודש, כאן בשינוי בעלים. ועוד י"ל דאפי' גרסינן "רבא", רוצה ליישב דברי רב לכולהו אמוראי דהתם. ולפי' ר"ת קשה, דנראה דרב משרשיא תלמידו של רבא היה ולא של רבה. ועוד י"ל שרוצה רבא ליישב דברי רב משמיה דמבוג אפי' כרבנן דפליגי עליה דר"ש, דלית להו "זאת תורת". ורב משרשיא כשהקשה לו מר"ש, היה יכול להקשות ממתני' דמנחות, אלא ניחא ליה למיפרך מברייתא, דאפי' לר"ש דמכשיר, לא מ"זאת תורת" מכשיר. וכן משמע מפי' הקונטרס. ואע"ג דבפ' דם חטאת (לקמן זבחים דף צב.) דרשינן "תורה אחת לכל החטאות", וליכא מאן דפליג — היינו במידי דכתיבא בהדיא בחטאת גופה, דרשינן ליה לכ"ע, כגון הני דפרק דם חטאת; אבל שינוי קודש לא כתב בחטאת. ובריש איזהו מקומן (לקמן זבחים דף מח.) דדריש "תורה אחת לכל האשמות", וקאמר: הניחא למאן דאית ליה "תורת", אלא למאן דלית ליה "תורת" היינו לר"ש ולרבנן בריש מנחות (דף ג:) לרבא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 9b:5:1.english: "Rav Mesharshiyya raised an objection to Rava," etc. - This is puzzling: What is the difficulty? It is Rava himself who explains the reasoning of Rabbi Shimon at the beginning of Menachot (3b) [as derived from] "This is the law of" (zot torat)! And Rabbeinu Tam says that here we read "Rabbah," and Rabbah is consistent with his own reasoning, as he answers there: Here it refers to a change of sanctity, and here it refers to a change of owners. Furthermore, it can be said that even if we read "Rava," he wants to reconcile the words of Rav with all the Amoraim there. But according to the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam it is difficult, since it appears that Rav Mesharshiyya was a student of Rava and not of Rabbah. Furthermore, it can be said that Rava wants to reconcile the words of Rav, in the name of Mavog, even according to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Shimon and do not hold [the derivation of] "This is the law of." And when Rav Mesharshiyya objected to him from Rabbi Shimon, he could have objected from the Mishnah in Menachot, but he preferred to refute [him] from a baraita, [to show] that even according to Rabbi Shimon, who deems [such offerings] fit, he does not deem them fit from "This is the law of." And so it is implied from the explanation of the Kuntres (Rashi). And although in the chapter of Dam Chatat (below, Zevachim 92a) we derive "one law for all sin offerings," and there is no one who disagrees — that is [because] with regard to something written explicitly in the sin offering itself, we derive it according to everyone, such as those [laws] of the chapter of Dam Chatat; but a change of sanctity is not written regarding the sin offering. And at the beginning of Eizehu Mekoman (below, Zevachim 48a), where it derives "one law for all guilt offerings," and says: This works well according to the one who holds "law" (torat) [is a source for derivation]; but according to the one who does not hold "law," that is, Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis at the beginning of Menachot (3b), [it is difficult] according to Rava.

Zevachim 9b:16.english: Rav says: A sin offering that one designated to atone for consuming chelev, that one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering brought for consuming blood, or for the sake of a sin offering brought for engaging in idol worship, is fit; the act of slaughtering is not considered a deviation from the type of offering.
